record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Hopf minimizers on positive-curvature space forms
record.original_question: Let M be a complete (2m+1)-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive curvature that is not the sphere, and consider smooth vector fields on M of fixed constant length r > 0. Is the infimum of the volume functional over such vector fields attained exactly by Hopf vector fields?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 On a complete .(2m + 1)-dimensional manifold M of constant curvature
the infimum of the volume of vector fields of constant length is attained exactly by Hopf vector fields.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m \geq 1$ be an integer and let $M$ be a complete $(2m+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive sectional curvature that is not isometric to the round sphere (so $M$ is a non-trivial quotient $S^{2m+1}(\rho)/\Gamma$ with $\Gamma \neq \{\mathrm{Id}\}$). For a smooth vector field $V$ on $M$, regard $V$ as a section of the tangent bundle and equip $TM$ with the Sasaki metric; the volume of $V$ is then defined as
$$\mathrm{Vol}(V) \;=\; \int_M \sqrt{\det\!\bigl(I + (\nabla V)^t (\nabla V)\bigr)} \, dv_M,$$
or equivalently as the volume of the submanifold $V(M) \subset TM$. Fix a constant $r>0$ and consider the class $\mathcal{V}_r(M)$ of smooth vector fields $V$ on $M$ with $\|V\|\equiv r$ everywhere. A Hopf vector field on $M$ is a unit-length (or, after rescaling, length-$r$) vector field tangent to the fibers of the Hopf fibration on $S^{2m+1}$, descended to the quotient $M$.

Question: Is it true that the infimum
$$\inf_{V \in \mathcal{V}_r(M)} \mathrm{Vol}(V)$$
is attained, and that the minimizers are exactly the Hopf vector fields of constant length $r$ on $M$?
artifact.category_tag: Volume of vector fields on space forms
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been established in dimension 3: on any complete 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive curvature (in particular on non-spherical quotients), the unit vector fields of minimum volume are exactly the Hopf vector fields, via calibration arguments. For higher odd dimensions $2m+1 \geq 5$, only stability results are known (Hopf fields are stable critical points on non-trivial quotients), and the full minimization statement appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Volume minimising unit vector fields on three dimensional space forms of positive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: The rigidity of Hopf vector fields as volume minimisers among unit vector fields is extended to any complete three dimensional manifold of positive constant curvature.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved in dimension 3 for all complete space forms of positive constant curvature.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Unit Hopf Vector Fields on Quotients of Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: In all other quotients (space forms of positive curvature) the Killing vector fields of constant length are stable critical points of the volume functional.
status_evidence.claim: In higher odd dimensions, Hopf fields are known to be stable critical points on non-trivial quotients, but the global minimization claim is not established.

status_evidence.title: On the volume of a unit vector field in 3 dimensions via calibrations
status_evidence.snippet: The minimal volume vector fields on S^3(r) are the Hopf vector fields, proved via calibration theory.
